text:
kevin: Heads up — seeing a spike of schema-warning / nonfatal validation messages from the toolhook runtime in prod (since ~08:15 UTC). Not full rejects but lots of 'missing required key' and 'type mismatch' warnings.

mira: @kevin can you paste an example? is this across a single model or routed ones? :eyes:

kevin: pasted a compact excerpt:
```
{
  "tool_response": {
    "action": "charge",
    // expected 'amount' but got null
  }
}
```
Mostly from the region-us route which hits the v3-toolhook adapter + model-A (quantized).

sara: saw the alert from onboarding dashboards. Spike correlates with a canary rollout that bumped the strict_schema flag to 0.8 for 5% slice.

oren: quick question — are these counting against customer quota like full responses? or do warnings get charged differently?

jay: right now, any successful generation (even with schema warnings) consumes normal tokens. We only mark evaluation telemetry as 'schema_warning' but charge is unchanged.

mira: That's the UX bug — customer sees degraded downstream behavior but same invoice. Ops will get paged but the app owner won't know why.

kevin: It's also affecting routing: the orchestrator treats these as successful and routes future requests to same model variant; if warnings accumulate, we should probabilistically fall back to permissive model or alternate region.

oren: Suggest we add a nonfatal metric that increments a separate quota bucket (schema_warnings) so customers and console can surface it without touching billing yet. We can then roll a change to make severe warnings billable after a decision.

mira: implementation-wise we need 3 things: (1) telemetry enum changes in adapter -> 'ok'|'warning'|'reject', (2) console dashboard tile for warnings per route/model, (3) routing policy that checks recent warning rate and de-prioritizes variant.

jay: for (3) it's tricky — routing is latency/cost-first today. We could add a penalty score for warning_rate > threshold. But that adds a control plane signal we don't have in the real-time path. Might need sampling to keep overhead low.

kevin: can we piggyback on the existing profiler stream (we already send a 1% sampled inference trace)? Add a warning flag to those traces first and build SLA dashboards from sampled data.

mira: agree start with sampling to prove usefulness. But customers asked for near-real-time alerting when a rollout causes toolhook schema drift — sampling may be too slow for 5% canaries.

oren: alternative: do lightweight increment in edge (increment a warning counter to statsd), then roll up quickly. That keeps path minimal. We already do token counters there.

jay: watch for cardinality — we need to index by org, route, model, and variant. Adding heavy labels may push our metrics backend. Keep tags coarse initially (org+route).

sara: console UX: customers need clear language: "toolhook returned partial/ambiguous response" + link to example and suggestion: retry with fallback variant / relax schema. Also allow mute for noisy third-party tools.

kevin: on the API side, we should expose a header like `X-Redwood-Schema-Warn: 1` in proxied responses so downstream infra and customers can detect without parsing body.

mira: +1. Also add structured telemetry event `schema_warning.v1` emitted to the event stream for downstream analytics (again low-cardinality).

oren: one more open debate: should schema warnings increment quota consumption at reduced rate? e.g., only bill 25% of tokens for a warning. That could be exploited if not gated.

jay: I'd be wary — customers might intentionally trigger warnings to lower cost. If we go this route, tie reduced billing only to warnings that still pass an automated quality check. Hard to define.

kevin: proposal: for now treat them as normal charge, expose warnings in billing preview and alert owners. After 2 weeks data, revisit reduced charge for 'minor' warnings with strict heuristics.

mira: rollout plan:
- stage 1 (today): add statsd counter + sampled trace flag + console read-only tile for warnings
- stage 2 (48h): implement routing penalty and canary rollback hook if warning_rate > X% for Y mins
- stage 3 (2w): evaluate billing changes if we have good quality labels

sara: can we also add a small canary-level guard: when strict_schema is on for a slice, if warnings exceed 10% within last 5m, revert slice to previous config and post a deploy note? That'd avoid operator lag.

oren: automation is fine but we need safety — revert only the slice, not entire model. Ensure deploy-bot annotates reason.

deploy-bot: Canary monitor: detected rule match for canary slice 5% on variant v3-toolhook. Auto-rollback scheduled in 2m unless acked by @sara or @kevin.

kevin: acked — hold rollback for 2m while we capture logs.

mira: action items: I'll add statsd counter PR (edge) and draft the console tile spec. @jay can you prototype routing penalty? @sara can you tune the canary rollback thresholds?

jay: will prototype a penalty module using an exponential backoff on score with warning_rate as input. Keep it disabled behind a feature flag.

sara: I'll lower the strict_schema canary to 1% until we have telemetry and dashboards.

kevin: thanks all. Let's reconvene in #eng-platform in 30m with PR links. If someone sees other affected routes ping here. :thumbsup:
